summary: Douglas County lookout on Scott Mountain near Roseburg, rebuilt several times from 1911 onward and destroyed in the Archie Creek Fire in September 2020.

facts.design: Tower with a live-in cab (35 ft, 1947 per firelookout.com); the register describes a 30-foot flat-roofed cab with catwalk from 1957
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the Archie Creek Fire in September 2020; the register and firelookout.com both say so

staffing.status: Staffed every summer into the late 2000s, per firelookout.com; an automated detection camera then took over spotting

events.note: First log cabin, per the register and firelookout.com; the Rex page dates the first lookout service to 1914
An assistant stationed at Point Lookout on the summit, per a Roseburg Review item quoted on the Rex page
50-foot pole tower with observation cab, per firelookout.com
New 50-foot tower, per a 1931 Oregon Department of Forestry annual report quoted on the Rex page
C.C.C. crews built a 50-foot tower and a 14-by-16 log cabin (Corvallis paper); the register instead describes a 100-foot wooden tower
Ranger at the lookout telephoned Roseburg that a missing 13-year-old had reached safety there
Station badly wrecked, apparently by a bolt of lightning (Rex page, May 27, 1942 Roseburg News-Review item)
Two women set off to take charge of the lookout for the summer (Roseburg News-Review, July 7, 1944)
Lookout Marcelene Moore noticed a fire in the distance shortly after midnight; a crew contained it before the heat of the day
Lookout replaced at a cost of $1192.36 (Rex page); firelookout.com dates a 35-foot timber tower with live-in cab to 1947
Register says the 100-foot tower was replaced by the present 30-foot ODF flat-roofed cab
Radio tower fell onto the lookout house in late December and damaged it
Tower and cabin completed for fire season, mostly built from two salvaged lookouts
Date registered February 24, 1996 per the National Historic Lookout Register
Lookout and related detection camera destroyed in the Archie Creek Fire, September 2020

corrections.proposed: omit until the height of the structure standing in 2020 is confirmed
corrections.why: 15.2 m is 50 ft, which matches the 1928-1933 pole tower. The register describes a 30-foot cab and firelookout.com a 35-foot tower for the structure that burned in 2020.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date the first log cabin to 1911. A 1914 Rex page note says the site was the first lookout put in service by the Douglas County Fire Patrol Association. The story reports both.

The register says a 100-foot wooden tower in 1933. The Rex page has a 50-foot tower in 1931 and a 50-foot tower with a 14 x 16 cabin built by C.C.C. crews in 1933. firelookout.com has a 50-foot pole tower in 1928. The story does not pick one.

The register dates the flat-roofed cab to 1957, firelookout.com dates a 35-foot timber tower to 1947, and the Rex page dates a tower mostly built from two salvaged lookouts to 1977. All three agree it burned in 2020.
The register says near Roseburg, firelookout.com says 18 miles northeast of Roseburg, and a 1914 Roseburg paper says 25 miles east of Roseburg.
The register gives 4,160 ft (1,268 m) and firelookout.com gives 4,250 ft. The brief's 1268 m matches the register.

notes_for_editor: Heavy source conflict on build dates and tower heights; the story names the conflicts and does not pick winners. The brief's height_m 15.2 (50 ft) matches the earlier pole tower, so the correction proposes omitting it. No source describes what remains on the summit today, and access is unknown. The 1933 panorama note on the Rex page calls the site Scott Mountain, and the story uses that name. firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum, Dave Bula and Howard Verschoor, but no image URLs were captured, so no photos are listed.
